proven_facts: Langton's ant was introduced by Christopher G. Langton, 'Studying artificial life with cellular automata', Physica D 22(1-3):120-149, October 1986 (doi:10.1016/0167-2789(86)90237-X); he called them 'vants' and never wrote '10,000', '104' or 'highway'.

Theorem (Bunimovich and Troubetzkoy, J. Stat. Phys. 67:289-302, 1992, doi:10.1007/BF01049035): for every initial configuration the ant's trajectory is unbounded. Popularly misnamed the 'Cohen-Kong theorem' (Stewart, Scientific American 271(1):104-107, July 1994); the misattribution is stated by Gale, Propp, Sutherland and Troubetzkoy, Math. Intelligencer 17(3):48-56, 1995.

Proof idea: the rule is reversible, so a bounded orbit would be periodic; the visited cell furthest up-and-right flips on every visit, so on alternate visits the ant must exit into a never-visited cell (Stewart 1994, Box 1).
Theorem (Troubetzkoy, Lewis-Parker lecture, Alabama J. Math. 21(2), 1997; cited by Gajardo et al. 2002 and Etse 2026): the set of cells exited infinitely often has no corner.

Theorem (Gajardo, Moreira, Goles, Discrete Applied Mathematics 117:41-50, 2002, doi:10.1016/S0166-218X(00)00334-6): a single ant on a finite configuration can evaluate any boolean circuit, so predicting it is P-hard; universality holds only with an infinite periodic configuration.

Theorem (Gale, Propp, Sutherland, Troubetzkoy 1995): generalized ants whose rule string has the even run-length property (e.g. LRRL, LLRR) return to bilateral symmetry for ever and never build a highway.
Theorem (Etse, arXiv:2606.26677, June 2026): the ant escapes any n x n domain within (n+1)! steps; exact confinement maxima S(n,n) = 1, 6, 17, 46, 85, 164, 262, 488, 679 for n = 1..9.

The highway has period 104 and drift (+-2,+-2) per period, speed sqrt(2)/52 (Boon, J. Stat. Phys. 102:355-360, 2001); the exact empty-grid onset 9977 is recorded in OEIS A261990 and Tokarz arXiv:1807.08789 and agrees with this repo with zero mismatches.

The highway conjecture (Gajardo et al. 2002: 'For any initial configuration with finite support, the ant eventually starts building the periodic highway, in some unobstructed direction') is OPEN as of June 2026 (Lutfalla arXiv:2505.05426; Gajardo, Lutfalla, Rao, Natural Computing 24:497-509, 2025; Etse arXiv:2606.26677).
open_status: OPEN. Unboundedness is proven for every initial configuration (Bunimovich-Troubetzkoy 1992), but whether every finite configuration leads to the 104-step highway has never been proven or refuted. Our 41,835,387 simulated runs (every pattern in boxes up to 5x5, 4.73 million random boxes up to 512x512, 3.48 million adversarial runs) all reached a certified highway; this is evidence, not proof.
